dedupe_keys.name: cedss 3 4 community energy demand social simulator

description: CEDSS is an agent-based social simulation of domestic energy demand in communities of about 100 to 250 households, such as a village or an urban or suburban estate. It rests on a 2010 survey of households in Aberdeen and public data on energy use trends, prices, energy-using and energy-saving equipment and household finances, with goal-framing theory as its theory of behaviour. It is calibrated by winding surveyed households back to 2000 and running forward to mid-2010 to compare with the survey, and can then be run forward under different assumptions. Version 3.4 was published by Nicholas Mark Gotts and J. Gary Polhill on CoMSES in July 2016. Coverage: Scottish communities. Access: free NetLogo code on CoMSES. Licence: GPL-3.0. Caveats: parameterised on one Scottish survey. Simulation uses are future domestic energy demand scenarios for neighbourhoods under price, policy and technology changes. Related records: HERB and the NIER retrofit model.
inputs: Trends in energy use, prices, equipment and household finances
name: CEDSS 3.4: Community Energy Demand Social Simulator
outputs: Domestic energy demand and household equipment trajectories to and beyond 2010
